svg.title: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate: DevSkim flags an insecure address on a developer's machine as in CI, and still skips the project's tmp folder
svg.text: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate
Scenario: DevSkim flags an insecure address on a developer's machine as in CI, and still skips the project's

g.text: Given a generated project holds an http:// address in its source and a copy in its own tmp
A project generated from the toolbox holds the same line twice: src/fetch.js reads its data from an http:// address, and
tmp/scratch.js, a scratch file in the project's own tmp folder, is a copy of it.
Below them, DevSkim's settings: the folders it skips. The tmp entry, **/?*/tmp/**, wants a folder name before tmp: it
matches the project's own tmp folder, never a tmp folder the project sits in.
Then on the developer's machine DevSkim flags the address in the source and skips the copy
The developer runs MegaLinter with DevSkim alone, then reads the findings back from the report that run wrote.
MegaLinter mounts the project under /tmp/lint, a path that starts with tmp.
The finding fails the run, so task ends on "exit code 201", as the same scan does in CI. The report holds one finding:
DS137138, an insecure URL, in src/fetch.js, and nothing in tmp/scratch.js. The test also scans the same files where CI
puts them, under /builds: DevSkim flags the same file there.
